fullDescription:
The Council is seeking 1 (ONE) fully maintained contract hire of one new battery-electric medium panel van.
Suppliers must submit separate quotations for 36-month and 60-month lease arrangements, based on 7,500 miles per annum.
Both contract durations will be independently evaluated using the published award criteria of 60% price and 40% quality. A Most Advantageous Tender (MAT) will be identified for each duration.
The Council has no preferred contract duration and reserves the right to award one contract only, selecting either the 36-month or 60-month arrangement in accordance with the published evaluation methodology.
The final award recommendation will be considered by Full Council in January 2027.
Tender prices will be evaluated excluding VAT. The estimated contract value, including VAT, will be declared separately for statutory procurement purposes.
The successful supplier must provide a fully converted, compliant and operational vehicle no later than 1 April 2027.

fullDescription:
Erewash Borough Council (EBC) have started work on a new Local Plan, which will be drawn up using the National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF), published in August 2026. The Council's Planning Policy team is embarking on an evidence base gathering exercise so that a new Local Plan can be adopted in the 30-month period which started after Gateway 1 was passed in October 2026, in line with Government objectives on speeding up plan-making. The Council's Green Space Strategy, which was adopted in 2009 and reviewed in 2018 (copies are available on request) is now out of date, and accordingly, to aid the Local Plan's preparation, a new study which includes a review of the current status of local green space within the borough and establishes local standards for green space provision in the form of a green space strategy across a period to 2040 is required.
Full details can be found within the invitation to tender documents.

The Spherical Tokamak for Energy Production (STEP) programme aims to deliver a prototype fusion energy plant by 2040, while also developing a robust fusion supply chain and a pathway to commercial fusion. Achieving this vision requires the delivery of an unprecedented and complex engineering design, alongside a major infrastructure project involving a large and diverse supply chain, all on an ambitious timeline.

The STEP programme directly supports the UK Government’s strategic objectives in clean energy innovation, energy resilience, and global technological leadership. Fusion energy is recognised as a potential transformative low-carbon energy source, offering long-term reductions in reliance on fossil fuels and mitigating exposure to volatile international energy markets.

fullDescription:
Cefas' laser sizer has reached the end of its useful lifespan. Replacement parts are no longer being manufactured and are becoming increasingly difficult to source. The equipment measures the fine sediment fraction, which is essential for particle size analysis. This analysis is used across most Sedimentology projects, and the resulting data supports several other areas of work within Cefas, externally and internationally.
Scope of Requirements:
Cefas requires the supply, delivery, installation and commissioning of a laser diffraction particle size analyser and an image-based particle shape analyser, both using wet dispersion, together with all software and licences needed for operation and data processing, all essential accessories and components, and user and routine-maintenance training. Cefas will provide the PC and monitor required to operate the instrument(s).
1. Technical Requirement
1.1 The laser Diffraction measurement range must extend from 0.2µm or smaller to 2mm or greater.

fullDescription:
About the VRU
The London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU), hosted within the Mayor's Office for Policing and Crime (MOPAC), pioneers a partnership-based public health approach to tackling violence rooted in prevention and early intervention. Since 2019, the VRU has invested in over 550,000 targeted interventions for young people across London.
Project Background
The VRU takes a public health approach to violence reduction, recognising that prevention requires action at different stages. Primary prevention seeks to change the conditions that make violence more likely, strengthening protective factors before violence occurs. Secondary prevention responds when risk or violence is emerging, aiming to interrupt risk and prevent escalation. Tertiary prevention focuses on reducing the harm caused by violence, supporting recovery and reducing the likelihood of further violence. These approaches are complementary, forming part of a wider response to violence and exploitation.

fullDescription:
Corby Closed Landfill is located on the northern outskirts of Corby. The landfill covers approximately thirteen (13) hectares. The volume of waste deposited into the site is unknown but is estimated to be in the order of 1.4Mm3 to a depth of around sixteen (16) metres. The buried waste produces landfill gas and leachate. The site has no form of impermeable containment and as such is considered to be a "dilute and disperse" site. The Council has a statutory duty under the Environmental Protection Act 1990 to manage the risks posed by the gas and leachate emissions produced on site.
The procurement of the Closed Landfill Site Operations and Maintenance will enable the Council to continue to fulfil its statutory obligations under Part 2A of the Environmental Protection Act 1990 and remain compliant with the site's Environmental Permit and Trade Effluent Consent.

Energy Coast West Cumbria Limited, trading as BEC, invites tenders for the design, manufacture and supply of a factory-integrated, modular Adiabatic Compressed Air Energy Storage (A-CAES) demonstrator plant for the BEST CAES project at Westlakes Science Park, West Cumbria.

fullDescription:
Energy Coast West Cumbria Limited, trading as BEC, invites tenders for the design, manufacture and supply of a factory-integrated, modular Adiabatic Compressed Air Energy Storage (A-CAES) demonstrator plant for the BEST CAES project at Westlakes Science Park, West Cumbria.
The requirement comprises an above-ground, transportable system incorporating compression, thermal storage, expansion equipment, compressed-air storage vessels, power electronics and controls, together with specified testing, documentation, training and warranty support. Required performance includes 0.333 MW charging, 1.0 MW discharge and a minimum electrical round-trip efficiency of 80%.
The maximum contract budget is £1,600,000 excluding VAT, with operational handover required by 30 June 2028. Long-term paid maintenance and supplementary rapid-response hardware are excluded from this award. The procurement will follow an open procedure and is subject to funding, planning permissions and necessary approvals.

The North, Central and East London Regional Partnership (NCEL RP), led by Islington Council, is seeking to appoint a Higher Education Institution (HEI) to co-design, develop and deliver the Step Up to Social Work Training Programme for Cohort 10.
The successful provider will deliver a bespoke, high-quality, Social Work England approved programme at Postgraduate Diploma level, with a pathway to master’s level study available following successful completion.
The programme will:
lead to the award of a Postgraduate Diploma in Social Work;
enable graduates to register with Social Work England; and
prepare trainees for practice within statutory children’s social work settings.
The programme itself will run for 15 months. The appointed HEI will also support the Regional Partnership with assessment and recruitment, trainee onboarding and pre-employment checks, curriculum design and programme planning, and securing the necessary Social Work England approval prior to programme commencement.

fullDescription:
The requirement
Islington Council is establishing a Flexible Framework for a period of eight years, with an estimated start date of October 2027.
A 'flexible framework ' is a contractual arrangement between Islington Council, as the contracting authority, and a number of providers. The purpose is to establish the quality requirements, pricing, and terms and conditions of providing the specified services during a given period of time. The council can then purchase services via the flexible framework from the successful providers. These are called 'call-off' contracts. The quantity and configuration of services purchased through the flexible framework is defined by the council, in response to local demand, and can change during the period of the framework.
Services will be procured under the flexible framework based on presenting demand, available funding, and availability of suitable buildings for accommodation-based services.

fullDescription: The Youth Drama Programme is a cross-border, cross-community peace-building initiative for 90 young people aged 16–21 years, delivered in three tranches of 30 participants between 1 December 2026 and 31 March 2028. The programme is designed to bring together young people from communities across the border region to develop meaningful relationships, increase understanding of different backgrounds and identities, and build confidence through shared creative experiences. Participants will take part in a structured programme of drama-based workshops that use theatre and the creative arts as a medium for dialogue, collaboration and personal development. Through facilitated activities, participants will explore themes including identity, culture, belonging, respect, inclusion and positive relationships while developing communication, teamwork, leadership and performance skills.

description: Open Mosaic Habitat (OMH) is recognised as a high distinctiveness Priority Habitat; which is very difficult to recreate or replace if destroyed. Under S41 NERC Act OMH is protected and Local Planning Authorities require rigorous mitigation if impacted via development. The demand for OMH mitigation opportunities is also intrinsically linked to the planning process and decision-making. This research project will map OMH resource across the Tees Estuary to develop an understanding of the types of O
fullDescription: Open Mosaic Habitat (OMH) is recognised as a high distinctiveness Priority Habitat; which is very difficult to recreate or replace if destroyed. Under S41 NERC Act OMH is protected and Local Planning Authorities require rigorous mitigation if impacted via development. The demand for OMH mitigation opportunities is also intrinsically linked to the planning process and decision-making. This research project will map OMH resource across the Tees Estuary to develop an understanding of the types of OMH across the area, identify areas of OMH not currently mapped and identify whether there have been changes in OMH resource over time. The research project will also collate species records to identify important species using the OMH resource and determine whether there are any characteristic OMH communities. Finally, this work will identify opportunities to maintain and enhance the OMG resource and produce a prioritised list of actions.

The furniture will be required across a range of areas, including the Customer Service Centre, meeting and interview rooms, waiting areas, self-service facilities and staff offices.
The Council is seeking high-quality, durable and accessible furniture that meets the operational requirements of each space while complementing the character of the Gra
fullDescription:
Watford Borough Council is seeking quotations for the supply, delivery, assembly and installation of furniture for the refurbished Watford Town Hall. The furniture will be required across a range of areas, including the Customer Service Centre, meeting and interview rooms, waiting areas, self-service facilities and staff offices.
The Council is seeking high-quality, durable and accessible furniture that meets the operational requirements of each space while complementing the character of the Grade II listed building. Suppliers are encouraged to recommend alternative products, dimensions or configurations where these would provide a more suitable or cost-effective solution.
The successful supplier will be responsible for the delivery and installation of all agreed furniture, ensuring that the building and newly refurbished areas are protected throughout the process. All furniture must be fully installed and ready for use by 15 February 2027, in accordance with the specification.

fullDescription:

The Framework will include a range of delivery models, including Development Agreements (DA), Joint Ventures (JV), Special Purpose Vehicles (SPV), Limited Liability Partnerships (LLP) and pre-development and feasibility support services.

fullDescription:

fullDescription:
In June 2026, the Borough Council of King’s Lynn and West Norfolk (the Council) started the process of producing a new Local Plan, which will cover the period 2026-2044.  To support the Local Plan preparation, the Council will need to renew or update its current evidence base, including undertaking a Habitat Regulations Assessment (HRA).
HRA is a legal requirement for the preparation of development plan documents (including the Local Plan), under Part 6 of the Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017, as amended (sections 63-64).  These require the “competent body” (in this case, the Council/local planning authority) to must make an appropriate assessment of the implications of the new Local Plan for European sites (Special Areas of Conservation/ Special Protection Areas/ Ramsar sites) in and around the Borough, in view of each designated site’s conservation objectives.

description:

fullDescription:
The Office of Rail and Road (ORR) is the independent economic and safety regulator of Britain's railways. ORR is developing its capability to assess the efficiency, productivity and value for money of passenger train operations.
Historically, passenger services have been delivered through a range of Train Operating Companies (TOCs), each with differing operating characteristics, service patterns and cost structures. As most of the industry moves towards a more integrated railway structure, ORR requires a robust framework for understanding variations in train operating expenditure and for benchmarking performance across the railway. 
Previous analytical work has demonstrated that econometric benchmarking of the cost of passenger operators is feasible using Great Britain rail industry data and has identified several statistically significant drivers of operating costs. However, further work is required to strengthen understanding of the key cost drivers and the relationships between them

fullDescription:
The DRT scheme (Tiger on Demand) is a flexible service that provides shared transport to users who specify their desired location and time of pick-up and drop-off using an app or call centre.  It will offer travel to any location within each individual zone and interchange with fixed route public transport services at specific points.
The service will connect residents who have little or no access to regular and scheduled bus services to work, leisure, education and social wellbeing opportunities.
The Contractor is required to supply the required vehicle(s), drivers, supervisory staff, maintenance staff and cleaning staff, plus technology to enable integration with the back-office elements of the DRT scheme.
The number of vehicles for each zone is as follows:
East Cambridgeshire – 2 x 22 seat vehicles.
Fenland – 1 x 16 seat vehicle.
South Cambridgeshire – 2 x 16 seat vehicles.

fullDescription:
The Crisis Resilience Fund (CRF) is a national funding programme for local authorities in England, launched on 1 April 2026 and running to 31 March 2029. 
The primary objective of CRF is to firstly provide a safety net for those on low incomes who encounter a financial shock. A financial shock is a sudden, unexpected expense or drop in income that can place pressure on their budget and wellbeing
Secondly, is to invest in building local financial resilience to enable individuals and communities to better deal with crises in the long-term, reducing crisis need. Providing timely support so that people can manage pressures, maintain control and avoid being pushed into crisis or prevent crises from escalating
The CRF replaces the Household Support Fund (HSF) with the explicit intention of moving from short-term crisis mitigation towards prevention, financial resilience, and reduced reliance on emergency support.

title: Economic Analysis of Deer Management with a Focus on Venison Supply Chain Development in and around the New Forest National Park
description:
The New Forest National Park Authority, Natural England and Forestry Commission are working together to convene experts and stakeholders to produce a Protected Site Strategy (PSS) and Strategic Action Plan (SAP) for deer management for the New Forest National Park and surrounding area. 
A critical component of enabling sustainable deer management is the effective utilisation of venison. A well-functioning venison supply chain can help offset management costs, create economic incentives, and supp
fullDescription:
The New Forest National Park Authority, Natural England and Forestry Commission are working together to convene experts and stakeholders to produce a Protected Site Strategy (PSS) and Strategic Action Plan (SAP) for deer management for the New Forest National Park and surrounding area. 
A critical component of enabling sustainable deer management is the effective utilisation of venison. A well-functioning venison supply chain can help offset management costs, create economic incentives, and support local food systems and rural economies.
However, the venison supply chain in and around the New Forest is currently perceived as underdeveloped, with constraints in processing capacity, market access, coordination, and demand.
This commission seeks to understand the economics of deer management as a whole system, with a particular focus on the role and potential of the venison supply chain as a key lever for improving outcomes.

fullDescription:

fullDescription:
Trinity House (TH) holds the operation and maintenance responsibility for over 60 lighthouses around England, Wales, the Channel Islands and Gibraltar. These critical aids-to-navigation (AtoNs) include several Rock Tower lighthouses that require regular modernisation and ongoing maintenance.
Accordingly, Trinity House would like to investigate the feasibility of utilising jack-up and floating assets to avoid repeated journeys to these remote locations by helicopter to mobilise personnel, equipment and tools.
To support this investigation, it is important to have accurate bathymetric and topographic surveys of the surrounding area.
In order to ensure successful completion of all survey by the end of March 2027, Trinity House reserve the right to appoint a singular or multiple suppliers to fulfil this requirement.
As a result, suppliers are requested to submit individual costs for each location.

fullDescription:
Cold homes, damp, mould and fuel poverty are driving poor health outcomes, increasing pressure on healthcare services and deepening inequalities.

The London Borough of Lambeth Council seek to commission up to four local providers to deliver Supported Employment provision through the targeted Individual Placement and Support (IPS) ‘Place and Train’ model. fullDescription:
A key component of the FSA work is to reduce the burden of foodborne disease in the UK.  Campylobacter is the leading bacterial cause of foodborne disease in the UK, with chicken meat being the most common food source of exposure to this pathogen.  Campylobacter is widespread in chicken farms, with 60% of UK broilers flocks carrying the pathogen at the point they are slaughtered.  Interventions further down the food chain do not reliably eliminate this pathogen.  Therefore, reducing Campylobacter colonisation on broiler flocks and contamination on chicken meat is a priority area for the FSA as this will contribute towards reducing human exposure and subsequent reported cases of foodborne disease.
A clear evidence gap remains on whether probiotics can consistently affect Campylobacter levels in broilers, across commercial UK farms under routine production conditions, and what magnitude of log reduction is realistically achievable.

fullDescription:

fullDescription: Barnsley Metropolitan Borough Council is seeking to appoint a Provider to deliver an Integrated Carers Support and Prevention Service. The Service will provide support for unpaid carers aged 18 and over, together with low-level preventative support for adults aged 18 and over to help maintain independence, improve wellbeing and prevent, reduce or delay the need for statutory care and support services. fullDescription:
The Impact Facility at the University of Kent is looking to procure a High-Speed Spectrometer System for attachment on to a two-stage light gas gun as part of its new ERC funded project.
The Impact Facility has been operating for over 30 years, focusing on the laboratory-based simulation of hypervelocity impact events relevant to spacecraft and planetary science. fullDescription:
This is the re-procurement of the Earl’s Court Community Champions service on behalf of the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea, and the Maternity Champions services on behalf of Westminster City Council and the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea.
Community Champions (CCs) are local resident volunteers who are recruited, trained and supported to improve health, wellbeing and community cohesion within their communities. The programme demonstrates how residents, services and providers can work together to improve outcomes for communities. Champions act as trusted local connectors, supporting both short-term emergency responses, such as during the COVID-19 pandemic, and longer-term health promotion, prevention and community resilience.

fullDescription:
Applications are invited from organisations based in the voluntary and community sector to lead a project funded by the Plymouth Health Determinants Collaboration. (PHDRC). We know that throughout Plymouth, communities and groups have great conversations and collect lots of rich information describing people's experience of life in Plymouth. Some of the information is collected with a specific purpose in mind, other information is more unexpected but valuable and relevant. Community groups have told us that it is challenging to understand how this information can be shared to influence thinking and decision making, with those who have the potential to make use of the knowledge. Further exploration suggested that people are more likely to share their knowledge and views if they feel that it is likely to make a difference. fullDescription:
The Sports Councils commissioned and published the Transgender Inclusion in Domestic Sport Guidance in September 2021. The Guidance is supported by several background documents, including the Transgender International Research Literature Review 2021. In April 2025, the Supreme Court Ruling (For Women Scotland Ltd V The Scottish Ministers) ruled that, under the 2010 Equality Act, the protected characteristic of ‘sex’ means a person’s biological sex. The updated Equalities and Human Rights Commission Statutory Code of Practice for services, public functions and associations became legally binding on 5 August 2026 and provides guidance as to how the Equality Act 2010 should be applied.  
Following advice from legal counsel, and a literature review on the topic, the Sports Councils CEOs agreed that a full review is required.

fullDescription:
The Authority has a need for assurance vetting of Ocean Tankers under contract to the Authority, either directly, or obtained by fuel Suppliers for delivery to the Authority’s sites under the Authority’s fuel supply contracts.  The Authority has two ships on long term charter, which provide the majority of the Authority’s fuel transport requirement.  These ships will require annual TMSA. Under DDP, the supplier of the fuel is responsible for delivery, which normally involves that company chartering a ship on the spot market.  The Authority therefore requires an expert provider of vessel risk evaluation services to provide a vetting service. The estimated contract duration for this requirement is 5 years and will run from Februrary 2027 until February 2032.

fullDescription:

fullDescription:

fullDescription:
The Council are commissioning Care in the home services including a Carers home and community respite service across Staffordshire for Carers who have been assessed as having support needs. Respite Care and support enables Carers to take a break from their caring role and evidence suggests that this can help to achieve positive health, wellbeing and quality of life outcomes for Carers. Fewer Carers experienced mental health problems if they had taken a break since beginning their caring role.
The purpose of Care in the home and Carers home and community respite Services are to enable Service Users to remain in their own homes, living as independently as possible and to achieve and maintain their autonomy, independence, personal identity and assessed outcomes.
This Procurement is a 'flexible Platform Agreement' which will be commissioned under the Light Touch Regime (implemented through Regulations 74-77 of the Public Contract Regulations 2015).

fullDescription:
British Gurkha’s Nepal (BGN) current vehicle fleet requires replacing.
The north of Nepal is dominated by the Himalayan Mountain Range; this region is sparsely populated and requires reliable vehicles with off road capabilities. The middle band of the country is hilly and more densely populated, including the two largest cites, Kathmandu and Pokhara where two of BGN’s camps are situated.  The southern strip of the country, bordering India, is comparatively flat but again, densely populated.  Both regions also require transport capable of traversing in off road conditions, particularly in the monsoon season.  Roads throughout Nepal often lack tarmac, including in population centres.  The road quality varies drastically from tarmac to potholed dirt tracks. There is a requirement for 4 x 4 vehicles to ensure BGN can meet its outputs across all geographic regions.

fullDescription:
Universal Sleep Support Model (Bradford District and Craven)

The service provides training and material for the children and young people workforce and specialist one-to-one sleep clinics for parents of children, aged 2-11 years old who are experiencing sleep difficulties. Sleep practitioners work with families to create a personalised sleep plan for their child.

The service aims to provide a flexible tiered support for families in partnership with family hubs to promote good sleep habits and reduce the need for specialist support by intervening early.

The service supports the development of a sleep pathway for Bradford District & Craven and is delivered in line with NICE clinical guidance and guidelines:
CG170 Autism Spectrum Disorder in Under 19s: Support and management
NG87 Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder: diagnosis and management.

fullDescription:
The Mums Matter programme is a well evidenced, co produced intervention designed with mums for mums, directly addressing a significant service gap for women experiencing mild to moderate perinatal mental health difficulties. fullDescription:

fullDescription:
This is a notice of the Authority's intention to award the proposed contract for the Service to the existing provider pursuant to Regulation 9 (3) of the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023, Direct Award Process C. For the avoidance of doubt, the provisions of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 do not apply to this award and neither does Procurement Act 2023.
The Home and Settle Service operates as a non regulated support service, meaning it does not require delivery by a CQC registered provider. Its purpose is to assist adults with limited local support networks to return home safely and re establish daily routines after hospital discharge, without providing any form of personal care. Because the service focuses solely on practical, low level support, it is well suited to delivery within the voluntary sector, where trained volunteers can contribute to tasks that enhance independence, social connection, and community based recovery.

fullDescription: The Harbour provides specialist counselling and psychotherapy for adults affected by life‑threatening illness, either as patients, carers or loved ones, as well as for people bereaved within the last two years. fullDescription: Cruse Bereavement Care provides emotional and psychological support to children, young people and adults experiencing grief across Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire. The service aims to help people understand and manage their bereavement, recognising that while many adjust without specialist help, some are at increased risk of physical or mental health difficulties and benefit from structured support. Cruse operates through trained volunteers who undergo rigorous selection, accredited training and ongoing supervision. Individuals self‑refer and begin with an initial contact and an assessment to determine their needs and the most suitable form of support. Available interventions include telephone support, group information sessions, drop‑in groups, one‑to‑one bereavement support, occasional therapeutic groups and limited specialist support for children and young people. fullDescription:

fullDescription:
The Maritime and Coastguard Agency (MCA) is establishing a Dynamic Market for the provision of specialist technical, operational, scientific and advisory services in support of maritime, offshore energy, environmental response and security-related activities.
The Dynamic Market is intended to provide a flexible and compliant commercial mechanism to enable Contracting Authorities to procure multidisciplinary services in both planned and time-critical scenarios. This includes, but is not limited to, support for incident preparedness, response, stabilisation, recovery and post-incident assurance.
Services to be delivered under the Dynamic Market may include technical advisory, operational delivery, engineering support, scientific analysis, regulatory guidance and specialist consultancy. Requirements may arise in complex, high-risk and multi-agency environments, including maritime salvage, offshore intervention, well control, pollution response and other emergency or contingency situations

fullDescription:
Martin Gallier Project (MGP) supports Psychiatry Liaison, HTT and Crisis lines across the CWP footprint for people (16+)who are experiencing suicidal crisis and would benefit from non-clinical suicide interventions. 
The model is based around accessibility and no waiting lists ensuring timely support when it's most needed.  
Once the referral has been received by MGP, a dedicated Suicide Intervention Worker makes contact within 24 hours. A collaborative safety plan is created upon first contact to support immediate risk and face-to-face appointment are offered to ensure ongoing support. As soon as the individual begins to feel safer and more able to manage their immediate risk, they are supported to move forward into post intervention support, so there is flow through the pathway.

fullDescription:
The NEPO528 - British Sign Language DPS commenced on 24 May 2021 for a term of 60 months and was due to expire on 24 May 2026. 
The original Contract Notice for this DPS was published on 5 March 2021: 2021/S 000-004508. 
The purpose of this notice is to extend the period of validity of the DPS for a period of 27 months from  24 May 2026 to 31 August 2028. 
The value of the DPS remains unchanged and NEPO do not anticipate that the extension of the validity of the DPS requires variation to the published value.
NEPO528 - British Sign Language has been established as a 'Dynamic Purchasing System' under a flexible approached based on the concept of Regulation 34 via Schedule 3, under the principles set out in Regulation 74-77 ('The Light Touch Regime').
The opportunity can be accessed via the Open eTendering system. Suppliers wishing to be considered for this Pseudo Dynamic Purchasing System must register their expression of interest and submit a tender through the Open eTendering System.

Individual Service Funds (ISFs) were formally introduced in the Care Act (2014), as an option for commissioning self-directed support. They are a mechanism by which a person's personal budget, agreed by a Social Worker, can be held by a third party organisation (i.e. neither by the County Council nor the person) who is a trusted organisation accredited by the County Council to help the person find the care and support they need in the local community, be it access to Homecare, Day Services, a Personal Assistant (PA), equipment needs, live-in care, social prescribing or signposting to other services and voluntary organisations that will help them achieve their agreed outcomes, or indeed a combination of all of the above. fullDescription:

fullDescription: The Education Alliance are looking to establish a Dynamic Purchasing System for professional services in construction and premises contracts within the UK (excluding Scotland). The DPS Agreement will cover projects including, but is not limited to, new builds, extensions, refurbishments, housing builds, multi-complex builds, works covering the railway industry, infrastructure projects, etc. The procurement will be a single stage process following the Public Contract Regulations 2015 open procedure. The DPS agreement will be established and coincide with the recently awarded framework for professional services in construction and premises 2024 and will be coterminous in April 2028. The DPS will be split in to 22 categories, this DPS agreement is being advertised and tendered, so it can be utilised by all Public-sector bodies, including Charities in the UK (excluding Scotland). Please refer to document set for a full application process overview.

fullDescription:
This DPS will offer mobile diagnostic and/or treatment units to healthcare and/or other organisations in the UK public sector. These units within the NHS would increase capacity within organisations to help facilitate the delivery of the elective programme and to help with waiting lists, patient backlogs and lack of staff availability/space. fullDescription:

fullDescription:
East Riding of Yorkshire Council and Hull City Council have a statutory duty to provide education to children and young people. Where an education offer is not possible through a mainstream or specialist provision, interim tuition will be required to meet the needs of the child or young person.
This requirement will be met through 3 Lots:
•	Lot 1 – Face to Face Teacher
•	Lot 2 – Face to Face Teaching Assistant
•	Lot 3 – Online Tuition
The Open Framework is a two-stage process. Providers will first need to meet the evaluation criteria. The framework will be open for submissions all year round with new providers being evaluated and admitted at six monthly intervals. (September and March)
A competitive Call-off process through Yortender will be used to award contracts.
The Framework will run 01 September 2025 – 31 August 2029 years plus the option to extend for a further 2 years at the sole discretion of ERYC and HCC.
Initial closing date for applications 20 March 2025.

fullDescription:
Portsmouth City Council ('the Council') is inviting requests from suitably qualified suppliers to be admitted to a pseudo-dynamic purchasing system (DPS) arrangement to provide temporary accommodation services, ordinarily in Portsmouth but also in the surrounding area. 
Temporary Accommodation supports those at-risk of homelessness by providing short-term accommodation while a longer-term placement is found. 
COMMENCEMENT & DURATION
Any placements made under this DPS will be made from the 10th March 2025 onwards. The maximum duration of the DPS is approx. 4 years. The DPS arrangements will expire on 23rd February 2029 12:00 and no new placements will be made via the DPS beyond this date, although placements made before this deadline may continue.

fullDescription: Suppliers are invited to submit a tender for the supply, delivery, installation, service and maintenance of vending machines, vending products, consumables and associated products including a fully managed vending service and self-fill machine options.  Although this is a National agreement for Vending Services, Regional suppliers are welcome to bid for each Lot.  The agreement is a dynamic purchasing agreement (DPS) which means new suppliers can be added to the agreement throughout the life of the system (at intervals stated in procurement documents) as long as they pass the first stage tender process.  Once successfully on the DPS, over the life time of the system you may be invited to complete a second stage tender in order to bid for individual contracts.  The DPS consists of 7 Lots, details of lot structure is available in the procurement documents.  The timetable set out in the tender document is indicative only and issubject to amendment at any time.

description:
Warrington Borough Council is establishing a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) to procure Specialist Residential and Respite Services for adults aged 18-64 with complex needs. The DPS will provide a flexible and compliant route to secure high-quality placements and support services for individuals with learning disabilities, autism, mental health conditions, dementia, physical disabilities, and/or challenging behaviours.
The DPS will run from 1st March 2025 to 23rd February 2029, with no extension
fullDescription:
Warrington Borough Council is establishing a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) to procure Specialist Residential and Respite Services for adults aged 18-64 with complex needs. The DPS will provide a flexible and compliant route to secure high-quality placements and support services for individuals with learning disabilities, autism, mental health conditions, dementia, physical disabilities, and/or challenging behaviours.
The DPS will run from 1st March 2025 to 23rd February 2029, with no extensions beyond this date due to legal requirements under the Procurement Act 2023. The estimated total value is £65 million over the DPS term, though this is indicative and not guaranteed.
The DPS is divided into four Lots to match provider capabilities with service requirements:
Lot 1: Specialist Residential Care – In Warrington (long-term care)
Lot 2: Specialist Residential Care – Outside Warrington (long-term care)
Lot 3: Residential Respite – In Warrington (short-term/emergency care)
Lot 4: Reside

lots.title: Lot 1: Specialist Residential Care – In Warrington
lots.description: Providers will deliver long-term residential care and support for adults with complex needs within Warrington, focusing on enabling independence and improving well-being.

lots.title: Specialist Residential Care – Outside Warrington
lots.description: Providers will offer long-term residential care placements for adults with complex needs in locations outside Warrington, ensuring access to specialist care where local provision may not be suitable.

lots.title: Residential Respite Care – In Warrington
lots.description: Providers will offer short-term respite care, including planned and emergency stays, for adults with complex needs within Warrington, giving carers a break while supporting individuals in a safe environment.

lots.title: Residential Respite Care – Outside Warrington
lots.description: Providers will deliver short-term respite care, including emergency placements, for adults with complex needs outside Warrington, providing flexibility for families and access to specialist settings if required.

fullDescription:
Barnsley Metropolitan Borough Council (BMBC) wishes to establish a transport DPS for the provision of passenger transport for children and adults. BMBC has a statutory duty to provide home to school travel arrangements for eligible children to access their education for both SEN and non-SEN children as outlined in the Home to School/college Travel Assistance Policy. fullDescription: ARU is establishing the Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) to provide ARU with a compliant procurement route for the provision of private student residential accommodation to new ARU students. The DPS will provide one or multiple suitable buildings to ARU in order to fulfil our accommodation needs. When the DPS is established, ARU will be able to search for Potential Providers that match their requirements using: service category, room type and price and any other criteria deemed necessary and available within the standard search criteria. ARU will invite all Potential Providers admitted to the DPS to bid for the specific contract, via a call for further competition (mini-competition) but may impose further conditions which exclude some Potential Providers from a specific competition. The DPS will be open for a period of 3 years and applications to the DPS may be made at any time during this period.

fullDescription:
The DPS (Dynamic Purchasing System) for Major and Minor Construction Works (2025) provides a broad range of major and minor construction works to support ENP Members/Licensees.
These works include various installation works, responsive repairs works, maintenance works and new build works, predominantly to social housing, private domestic properties, public sector and commercial buildings but may extend to other property types that are owned or managed by ENP members/licensees.
Whilst the DPS would be UK wide, Contractors will be able to select particular regions that they operate in.
A DPS is a completely electronic process conducted in accordance with the Public Contracts Regulations 2015.

fullDescription:
The London Borough of Haringey ('The Council')is establishing a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) to procure and commission accommodation based Supported Living Services for vulnerable adults.  The Council invites suitably qualified suppliers of Supported Living Services to submit a request to participate in the DPS for the provision of the range of services to service users.
This will cover provision of service in users with Physical Disabilities, Mental Health issues, Learning Disabilities and  Positive Behavioral Services with various support needs due to issues around rough sleeping and homelessness..
These services relate to the statutory duties of the local authorities under the Housing Act 1996 Part VII as amended by the Homelessness Act 2002 and the Care Act 2015 to provide support based accommodation to vulnerable adults with varied support needs.

fullDescription:
Cumberland Council is looking to establish a Dynamic Purchasing System (“DPS”) for the provision of Passenger Transport Services which includes, but not limited to, Home to School, Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND), Pupil Referral Units, and Health, Care and Communities Transport.

Contracts are awarded during the second stage of the process. In stage two the council will invite Tenderers successfully admitted on the DPS to bid for contracts (routes).

fullDescription:
Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for the Business Model Innovation team.
The team have seen an increase in demand for projects over the last two years and are looking for external support for projects we do not have the capacity to cover. Although the ESC has existing procurement frameworks they are not entirely fit for purpose for this kind of work because:
•	they are more expensive to contract then our commercial day rate meaning outsourcing decisions do not stack up commercially 
•	we lose control of the ESC process and experience for partners
•	any insights or relationships developed can be lost to the 3rd party due to a lack of ESC involvement.

fullDescription:

fullDescription:

The DPS will provide TfGM with a selection of qualified operators to supply tendered services in areas where there is a social need that is not served by the commercial bus network.

Please note the tender documents will be made available at https://procontract.due-north.com/ from the 21st November 2024.
All contracts awarded under the DPS will follow further competitions which will commence early 2025.
Only qualified operators that are on the DPS will be invited to participate.

fullDescription:
The Authority (FLS) has established a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for Woodland Establishment across Scotland.
A Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) is an electronic system used to tender for services with a group of pre-qualified suppliers. FLS uses this system of pre-qualified suppliers to tender for Woodland Creation projects as and when they arise.
To submit a bid to join the DPS, suppliers need to submit a Single Procurement Document (SPD) through the DPS project on the Public Contracts Scotland – Tender (PCS-T) website. The SPD is a qualification response form which allows FLS to assess bidders’ suitability, experience, and capability to provide the services which may be required under the DPS. Only bidders that achieve a ‘Pass’ for all questions in the SPD are appointed to the DPS.
The DPS comprises 2 Lots; Commercial and Amenity, and Planting and Maintenance.
This DPS is extending the validity date from the 31st October 2024 until 31st October 2029.

fullDescription:
The service is to provide universal stop smoking services in the borough of South Tyneside through GP practices and community pharmacies. 
Providers will work in partnership with South Tyneside Council, specialist services and the NHS in a whole system approach focused on:
•	Delivering timely, evidence-based, personalised, proactive and fair stop smoking services in South Tyneside.
•	Providing high quality, person-centred and compassionate behavioural support which supports individuals to quit smoking & restart quit attempts after relapses.
•	Offering access to evidence-based pharmacotherapies / nicotine containing products, focusing on the most effective and popular options.
•	Delivering targeted and more intensive support using outreach methods to priority population groups.
•	Promoting prevention, early intervention, harm reduction, and making every contact count (MECC) principles.
•	Developing local strategies to reduce smoking prevalence, tackle smoking related health inequalities

fullDescription: The Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) will provide a database of Approved suppliers considered capable of carrying out professional consultancy services to a satisfactory standard. The nature and types of services that may be required may include, but are not limited to, those services identified by the CPV code and summarised in section II.2. The specific services cannot be clearly defined at this stage, however the nature and types of services that may be required may include, but are not limited to, buildings and civils professional consultancy services. The DPS is a 2-stage process: Stage 1 - All providers who meet the selection criteria within the online Questionnaire and are not excluded will be admitted to the DPS. New providers can also apply to join the DPS at any point during its lifetime. Stage 2 - Contracts are awarded during the second stage. A Call-Off competition will be put out inviting each approved provider on the DPS list relating to the particular Lot.

fullDescription:
This DPS will offer mobile diagnostic and/or treatment units to healthcare and/or other organisations in the UK public sector. These units within the NHS would increase capacity within organisations to help facilitate the delivery of the elective programme and to help with waiting lists, patient backlogs and lack of staff availability/space. Suppliers would work closely with healthcare organisations to deliver easily accessible treatments or diagnostics, either on hospital sites or closer to patients homes in more remote areas (for example at supermarkets, GP practices etc.). By working with healthcare organisations, suppliers will relieve pressure on services by improving access to treatments and bed space, reducing patient waiting times and freeing up clinical capacity. Units are usually provided in the form of vans or non-permanent units/cabins.

Scottish Water is looking to engage with potential Suppliers of Solar Panels through the use of a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS). fullDescription:
Merthyr Tydfil County Borough Council is establishing a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for the provision of a high quality and cost effective Education and Social Care Transport Service. The DPS Supplier Qualification Questionnaire (SQQ) will remain available for the duration of the DPS. The requirements will cover bus, taxi, minibus and wheelchair accessible vehicles. The DPS will be structured into the following 5 lots:
Lot 1: 4-8 seat vehicles
Lot 2: 9-16 seat vehicles
Lot 3: 17-49 seat vehicles
Lot 4: 50+ seat vehicles
Lot 5: Wheelchair accessible vehicles
The DPS will run for an initial period of 5 years with an option to be extended for a further period of up to 24 months (reviewable on an annual basis and subject to performance).
NOTE: The authority is using eTenderWales to carry out this procurement process. To access the tender documentation please visit https://etenderwales.bravosolution.co.uk

fullDescription: The Authority wishes to award an Approved Provider List for the Provision of Supported Internships (“the Contract”). fullDescription: The City of Doncaster Council is to establish a Flexible Procurement System (FPS) for the Provision of Children's Specialist Education Services under the light touch regime. The FPS for the Provision of Children's Specialist Education Services is part of the continuum of services that support children, young people, and their families. It provides a structured and organised approach that outlines the principles, guidelines, and strategies for providing specialist education provision to children and young people with unique learning needs or specific challenges such as school avoidance, trauma response behaviour or other emotional or behaviour concerns. This framework serves as a blueprint for designing, implementing, and evaluating educational programs that are tailored to address the diverse requirements of these children and young people, ensuring that they receive effective and targeted support in their learning journey.

fullDescription:
Due to the ongoing growth and development of the Open Banking market, Crown Commercial Service (CCS), as the Authority, intends to put in place an agreement for Open Banking Services for use by Central Government and the Wider Public Sector.
The Agreement will be a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS). This will be called RM6301: Open Banking DPS (Data, Digital Payments and Confirmation of Payee Services).
This agreement will provide a vehicle for Central Government and the Public Sector to source Open Banking Services, including but not limited to:
Digital Payment Services
Account Information Services
Confirmation of Payee (CoP) Services
This will be the first agreement for Open Banking Services CCS has developed. We intend to launch for supplier onboarding from late July with the DPS anticipated to go live for use in the Autumn.
The agreement is expected to run for 8 years and suppliers will have the opportunity to onboard throughout this duration.

fullDescription:

awardCriteriaDesc:
Surrey County Council (SCC) wishes to establish a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for the supply of services in respect of Independent Alternative Provision for children and young people with additional needs and disabilities for an initial period of 4 years + with optional further extension provisions for an additional 2 years + 2 years.
The services required fall under Schedule 3 of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 (PCR 2015). As a result, this procurement is undertaken under the 'Light Touch Regime' as detailed in Section 7 of PCR 2015.
This contract notice is for admission onto the DPS.
For each Lot/ sub-lot, there will be an ‘Admission’ stage, followed by a ‘Contracting’ stage.
Stage 1: Admission Stage – At this stage Bidders are invited to apply for admittance onto the DPS by submitting their responses via the Pass/Fail Selection Questionnaire (SQ) and, if passed, the evaluation of quality questions. If successful, Providers will be ‘admitted’ onto the DPS in the relevant Lots.
Stage 2: Contracting Stage – The Providers who meet the initial Admission criteria will be invited to bid for the relevant lots and/or sub-lots for individual placements or block contracts.
SCC intends to evaluate new applications to the ‘Admission’ stage twice a year. The Council reserves the right to revise the number of evaluation Rounds (‘opening ceremonies’) for Admission stage per year at its discretion to allow further applicants to apply in an emergency.
For the purposes of this Contract Notice, the overall estimated aggregate DPS value has been divided equally between each Lot however does not reflect the anticipated Lot spend. This will be determined based on the need of the individual at Stage 2: Contracting Stage and cannot be anticipated at this stage.
Admission stage evaluation will be based on 100% Quality.
The Council will reject any Bidder who scores a moderated score of 0 or 1 for any question.
Minimum Quality: Bidders should be aware that to be admitted onto this DPS, they must achieve a moderated qualitative evaluation score of no less than 60% out of the total percentage available for quality (60 out of 100); and a minimum moderated score of 2 will be required for all quality questions.
Pricing will be requested and will be binding for 2 years but will not be scored at admission stage. This pricing will be used at Stage 2: Contracting Stage. See ITT guidance for further information.
Stage 2 will be evaluated based on Quality and Price for all Lots and sub-lots. Full details will be included at Contracting Stage.
Once Providers are admitted onto the DPS, the ‘Contracting’ stage can be undertaken. Providers will be requested to respond to quality and price questions for the specific need to win the contract as outlined in the Referral Form.
Referrals will be published when the Contracting stage goes live.
Stage 2: Contracting Stage is divided into two routes:
Route 1: Direct Award
Route 2: Mini Competition
Route 1: Direct Award
When a placement is identified, the Council will send an Alternative Provision Referral Form to a Provider.
The Provider must return the Referral Form to the Council within 5 working days of receipt.
The Referral Form will allow the Provider to detail how they will best meet the outcomes of the individual as well as the price for the service.
The price submitted must be in line or lower than the price submitted at Admission Stage to the DPS.
As the DPS is being let under the Light Touch Regime (Regulation 76 (8) of the PCR’s 2015), the Council shall make Direct Award placements based on a number of factors including; the Provider that best meets the specific needs of the individual; and/or cost and value for money; and/or geographical location (if face-to-face); and/or availability of providers; and/or personal choice of the individual.
All awarded placements will be contractually bound by the Individual Alternative Provision Agreement (IAPA).
Route 2: Mini Competition
When a block contract or mini-competition is identified, Route 2: Mini- Competition will take place. The Council will invite all Providers admitted to the DPS under the relevant sub-lot(s) to express an interest based on the total number of referrals. The expression of interest will be time-bound.
Mini-Competitions will be evaluated based on Quality and Price. Full details will be included at Contracting Stage.
TUPE may apply at Stage 2: Contracting Stage. Full details will be included in the tender documents.
The bid deadline for the initial ‘Round’ for this DPS is 1st November 2023 at 12 Noon.
The time limit for receipt of tenders or requests to participate following the initial Round is 7 April 2028 following the initial 4 year term of the DPS.

The Council is looking to develop a Pseudo Dynamic Purchasing System (Pseudo DPS) for

providers in the local area and, therefore, are looking to commission provision in the
Wakefield, Leeds, Barnsley and Kirklees Local Authority areas.
Applicants who meet and pass the Application criteria will be admitted to the Pseudo DPS.
Please note that this is not a competitive process and there is no limit to the number of
Applicants who can be appointed.
Please note, Applicants who are successfully admitted on to the PDPS are not guaranteed to

fullDescription:
The Council of the Borough of Kirklees (the “Council”) is conducting this procurement exercise, in accordance with the Light Touch Regime of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 (SI 2015/102), and intends to establish an Electronic Market Place (“EMP”) with Providers with relevant experience and ability to provide Supported Living Services on a non-exclusive basis to Adults with eligible Social Care needs for the Council.
The EMP may be used by the Council and by the NHS Kirklees Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG) (subject to CCG governance approval).
The Council wishes to establish a Supported Living Services (SLS) EMP  to replace the current Framework Agreement.  As the current Framework Agreement does not allow new Providers to be able to join, the new SLS EMP will  allow new Providers to join.
awardCriteriaDesc: If a Contracting Body decides to source any of the Services through this EPM, then it may satisfy its requirements by allocating a Contract in accordance with the terms laid down in the EMP Information, Rules and Instructions document, included within the procurement documents.

fullDescription:
Lancashire County Council (the Authority) wishes to establish an open Provider List of Break Time and Short Breaks Providers who are suitable, capable and experienced to deliver the required services. This will greatly improve choice and the ability to meet the needs of children and young people with appropriate services.
Short Breaks Services ("the Services") are essential for children with disabilities, their parents and their carers, to ensure better outcomes and to prevent escalation of their needs, where possible.
The term 'short breaks' describes services that help adult parent/carers to more effectively provide care for their disabled child by providing them regular breaks

fullDescription:
Lancashire County Council (the Council) are leading on the procurement of an open Flexible Agreement for the Provision of Fostering Agency Placements. 
Since 2019 Blackburn with Darwen Council, Blackpool Council, Cumbria County Council and Lancashire County Council (BBLC) have been collaborating as part of a Department of Education funded project to improve the sufficiency of foster care placements across the authorities. By working together, the four Contracting Bodies have developed the Flexible Agreement which this procurement intends to establish, with the aim to influence the behaviour of these agencies in order to prioritise the Children from the four Contracting Bodies within the combined authorities' geographical footprint.
The Flexible Agreement will be a list of approved Independent Foster Care Providers.
It is intended that the Flexible Agreement will remain effect for 9 years, Service Contracts can be awarded as call-off contracts as detailed within the Invitation to Partic
